newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta Pool says wheat grades altered by frost.
newsitem.headline: Alberta Pool says wheat grades altered by frost.

text.p: Alberta Wheat Pool on Friday said it revised its estimates of grain and oilseed quality grades from last week because of frost during the harvest.

"Various stations from across the province reported frost and one station in crop district 15 (British Columbia's end of the Peace River Valley) reported a light dusting of snow in northern areas," AWP said in its weekly crop report.
About 51 percent of hard red spring wheat should grade No1 Canada Western Red Spring compared with 58 percent last year.
About 31 percent should grade No2 CWRS versus 31 percent last year, and 19 percent at No3 CWRS versus 10 last year.
About six percent should grade as feed wheat compared with one percent last year.

Twenty percent of barley should grade as malt compared with 23 percent last year. Seventy-one percent should grade as No1 CW compared with 70 percent last year and nine percent should grade No2 CW compared to six percent last year.

Eighty percent of canola should grade No1 Canada versus 77 percent last year while 16 percent should grade No2 C compared to 18 and three percent should grade No3 C compared to four percent and one should grade as sample, the same as last year.
